one_liner: Google's libjpeg62-compatible JPEG encoder/decoder tuned for quality per byte; not faster than libjpeg-turbo, and slower at decode.
what_it_does: A from-scratch C++ JPEG codec that exposes the libjpeg62 API under jpegli_* names and, on Linux-style targets, as a drop-in libjpeg.so.62.3.0, plus cjpegli/djpegli command-line tools. The encoder takes a JPEG XL style distance (or a libjpeg quality mapped to one), 8-bit, 16-bit or float input, and optional XYB-ICC mode. The decoder accepts 8-bit baseline, extended-sequential and progressive Huffman JPEGs and can emit 8-bit, 16-bit or float pixels.
how_it_is_fast: It is not built for speed: the design spends extra work on quality. The encoder does color conversion, subsampling and DCT in float (Highway SIMD, kernels capped at 8 float lanes) and adds adaptive dead-zone quantization driven by a masking field (fuzzy erosion over a pre-erosion image). The decoder gathers per-coefficient nonzero and abs-sum statistics and applies Price-Rabbani Laplacian dequantization biases, then runs float IDCT, upsampling and color conversion. Speed comes only from Highway runtime dispatch (SSE2 to AVX-512, NEON, SVE, RVV, WASM) and a streaming single-pass path for sequential fixed-Huffman encodes.
when_to_use: New web or archive JPEGs where bytes at a given visual quality matter more than encode CPU, and the output must stay plain JPEG for every decoder.
Linux services already linked against libjpeg62 that want jpegli's quality by swapping libjpeg.so.62 without code changes (libjpeg API only, not TurboJPEG).

Replacing mozjpeg trellis encodes on a CPU budget: oximg issue #61 timed jpegli at 534-1912 us against mozjpeg trellis at 10316 us per 512 px q80 encode, about 5.4x to 19x faster depending on jpegli settings (derived from page data).
Pipelines that need 16-bit or float input to the encoder or 16-bit/float output from the decoder, or XYB-ICC JPEGs.
when_not_to_use: Decode-throughput-bound workloads (thumbnailing, ML data loading): the only third-party number (oximg #61) puts jpegli decode 1.6-2.0x slower than libjpeg-turbo, with no methodology shown.

Encode-throughput-bound workloads that are fine with libjpeg-turbo quality: no source shows jpegli encoding faster than libjpeg-turbo, and its default tool settings (progressive level 2, optimized Huffman, adaptive quantization, 4:4:4) do the most work.

Code that uses the TurboJPEG API (tj*), arithmetic-coded, 12-bit, lossless or hierarchical JPEGs: the decoder accepts only SOF0/SOF1/SOF2 at 8-bit precision and the encoder errors on arithmetic coding and CCIR601 sampling.

Ingesting messy real-world files: issue #248 (open) reports djpegli rejecting progressive JPEGs with empty DHT segments ('DHT marker: no Huffman table found'), including 276 WhatsApp images from FODB that libjpeg-turbo-based decoders accept.

Projects that need versioned releases or a drop-in shared library on macOS or Windows: there are no tags or releases (issue #44 unanswered), and lib/jpegli.cmake builds libjpeg.so only when not APPLE, WIN32 or EMSCRIPTEN.

integration.form: static lib (jpegli-static, jpegli_* API) plus shared lib (libjpeg.so.62.3.0 drop-in on non-Apple, non-Windows targets) and CLI tools
integration.dependencies: Highway (third_party submodule or system libhwy), threads; libjpeg-turbo headers vendored for jpeglib.h/jmorecfg.h; tools add lcms2 or skcms, libpng, optional giflib, OpenEXR, sjpeg; tests need gtest and a system libjpeg
integration.min_toolchain: CMake 3.16+; C++17 when the compiler offers it (CMake falls back to C++14 or C++11); build breakages reported on macOS Sonoma (#55) and Fedora 42 (#133)
integration.platforms: any Highway target with runtime dispatch: x86-64 SSE2 to AVX-512, aarch64 NEON/SVE, PPC8-10, RVV, s390x Z14/Z15, WASM, scalar fallback
integration.thread_safety: not documented; libjpeg model of one compress/decompress object per thread, no internal multithreading found in lib/jpegli. decode_scan.cc writes edge-MCU padding blocks into a function-static sink_block shared by all decoder instances (a benign data race that thread sanitizers may flag).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — libjpeg62 API/ABI (jpeg_* symbols incl. jpeg_mem_src/dest, skip/crop scanlines, read/write_coefficients) but no TurboJPEG tj* functions, no arithmetic/12-bit/lossless decode, output pixels differ from libjpeg-turbo, and the .so is not built on macOS or Windows

gotchas: Defaults depend on the entry point: through the libjpeg API, jpeg_set_defaults gives sequential mode with fixed Huffman codes (kDefaultProgressiveLevel = 0 since commit eca9351, April 2023), which takes the streaming single-pass path; cjpegli and the extras EncodeJpeg API default to progressive level 2, optimized codes, adaptive quantization and no chroma subsampling, which buffer the whole image's coefficients and tokens. In oximg #61, settings alone on the same jpegli-sys 0.10.2 build move encode time 2.9-3.1x (progressive 4:4:4 AQ on 1812-1912 us vs baseline 4:2:0 AQ off 615-630 us, derived from page data).

Decoded pixels are not bit-exact with libjpeg-turbo: dequantization biases are computed from running statistics of the image's own coefficients and the pipeline is float, so golden-image tests written against libjpeg-turbo will fail.

The in-repo harness (tools/benchmark/benchmark_codec_jpeg.cc) has comparison traps: the pN parameter means jpeg_simple_progression for the libjpeg codec at p0 but sequential mode for enc-jpegli at p0; the cjpeg/mozjpeg path times a subprocess including process start and file I/O while jpegli is timed in process; and the Q (libjpeg_quality) option times an extra libjpeg encode plus a distance search inside the jpegli measurement.

Open, unreviewed PRs fix out-of-bounds bugs reachable through the library API with bad caller arguments: #242 (jpegli_crop_scanline 32-bit overflow leading to an out-of-bounds read) and #241 (jpegli_add_quant_table accepts which_tbl == 4 and writes 64 coefficients through a bogus pointer).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick jpegli over libjpeg-turbo only when smaller files at equal perceived quality matter more than CPU; keep libjpeg-turbo (or jpeg-nitro and zenjpeg for decode) when speed is the goal. Pick it over mozjpeg when you want a density-focused encoder at a fraction of trellis cost (oximg #61: 534-1912 us vs 10316 us), accepting that the density comparison rests on Google's own study ('Users prefer Jpegli over same-sized libjpeg-turbo or MozJPEG', not opened here).
verified_claims_summary: The repository publishes no speed numbers, and its benchmark doc is a leftover libjxl text about density metrics. The only measured numbers are third-party: oximg issue #61 (Zen 4, 512 px, q80, single-thread encode time on 1 logical CPU) kept libjpeg-turbo as its decoder because jpegli decoded 1.6-2.0x slower. It timed jpegli encodes at 1812-1912 us (jpegli-sys 0.10.2, progressive 4:4:4, AQ on), 960-976 us (baseline 4:4:4, AQ off), 615-630 us (baseline 4:2:0, AQ off) and 534-546 us (upstream 031a0077 with clang, baseline 4:2:0, AQ off), against mozjpeg trellis at 10316 us, with no libjpeg-turbo encode timing. A search snippet attributed to a libjpeg-turbo-users thread ('Jpegli', groups.google.com blocked here) says libjpeg-turbo was 2-8x faster than jpegli at baseline compression; this is unverified.
status_note: Active but thinly maintained: the last merged change is a Dependabot bump (2026-06-01, #236) while about ten bug-fix PRs from May-October 2026 sit unreviewed; BSD-3-Clause with a Google patent grant and no tagged release, so it is copyable but should be treated as a quality tool, not a speed win.
